cases.prevAction: I step down onto the landing.
cases.lastNarration: The boards of the landing give a little under your boots. A broad man with one sleeve pinned up leans against the rope post, watching the water. Off to one side, a small woman turns river-eels over a smoking firepit and does not look up.
cases.action: I ask the ferryman how much he charges to take me across.

cases.prevAction: I step down onto the landing.
cases.lastNarration: The boards of the landing give a little under your boots. A broad man with one sleeve pinned up leans against the rope post, watching the water. Off to one side, a small woman turns river-eels over a smoking firepit and does not look up.
cases.action: I wander over to the firepit and watch the woman turning the eels.

cases.prevAction: I ask the ferryman how much he charges to take me across.
cases.lastNarration: "Two coppers," he says, and holds out his one hand. When the coins are in it he nods at the raft tied to the post. "Both hands on the rope. She leans."
cases.action: I climb onto the raft and take hold of the rope.

cases.prevAction: I ask the ferryman how much he charges to take me across.
cases.lastNarration: "Two coppers," he says. He squints at the sky, then back at you. "Light's going. You crossing or not?"
cases.action: I say nothing and study the far bank for a long moment.

cases.prevAction: I find a stool at the bar.
cases.lastNarration: The Cinder and Crown is loud and warm. A round, red-cheeked woman bangs a tankard down in front of you without being asked. At the back table, a slight woman with a crooked grin is losing at dice to a well-dressed man who looks amused about it.
cases.action: I lean on the bar and ask the keeper what she has heard about the barrow.

cases.prevAction: I find a stool at the bar.
cases.lastNarration: The Cinder and Crown is loud and warm. A round, red-cheeked woman bangs a tankard down in front of you without being asked. At the back table, a slight woman with a crooked grin is losing at dice to a well-dressed man who looks amused about it.
cases.action: I sit down across from the well-dressed man and ask him what he is really after in the barrow.

cases.prevAction: I carry my drink to the back table.
cases.lastNarration: The two at the back table look up as you set your tankard down. The slight woman pulls her dice toward her; the man in the good coat makes room on the bench with a little bow.
cases.action: I raise my tankard to both of them and drink to the barrow being closed.

cases.prevAction: I read the notice board by the well.
cases.lastNarration: The notices flap in the wind off the wall. Most are old. The newest, nailed over the rest, is the keep's call for hands, and someone has scrawled a tally of names under it.
cases.action: I push open the door of the Cinder and Crown and head for the hearth.

cases.prevAction: I walk through the gate into the yard.
cases.lastNarration: The gate yard smells of smoke and wet stone. A gray-templed officer stands by the posted call for hands, arms folded. Near the well a broad man in plain mail polishes a shield, and a slight woman sits on the well's lip, swinging her heels.
cases.action: I salute the captain and ask what the bounty pays.

cases.prevAction: I salute the captain and ask what the bounty pays.
cases.lastNarration: "Gold for results," the captain says. "Nothing for stories." He looks you over. "And nothing at all if you go out there with steel that won't bite the dead."
cases.action: I ask the captain where I can get a blade that will cut the dead, and who makes them.

cases.prevAction: I walk through the gate into the yard.
cases.lastNarration: The gate yard smells of smoke and wet stone. A gray-templed officer stands by the posted call for hands, arms folded. Near the well a broad man in plain mail polishes a shield, and a slight woman sits on the well's lip, swinging her heels.
cases.action: I ask the man polishing the shield whether he will come with me to the barrow.

cases.prevAction: I walk through the gate into the yard.
cases.lastNarration: The gate yard smells of smoke and wet stone. A gray-templed officer stands by the posted call for hands, arms folded. Near the well a broad man in plain mail polishes a shield, and a slight woman sits on the well's lip, swinging her heels.
cases.action: I sit on a crate by the wall and check my pack and boots.

cases.prevAction: I walk down from the keep into the town.
cases.lastNarration: Ashford Square is half market, half argument. A woman in black stands alone by the well. On the steps of the hall, a heavy man with a chain of office talks loudly to anyone who will listen, and a well-dressed stranger leans on a stall, listening with a small smile.
cases.action: I read the notices pinned to the board by the well.

cases.prevAction: I walk down from the keep into the town.
cases.lastNarration: Ashford Square is half market, half argument. A woman in black stands alone by the well. On the steps of the hall, a heavy man with a chain of office talks loudly to anyone who will listen, and a well-dressed stranger leans on a stall, listening with a small smile.
cases.action: I go to the woman in black by the well and ask if I can help her.

cases.prevAction: I walk down from the keep into the town.
cases.lastNarration: Ashford Square is half market, half argument. A woman in black stands alone by the well. On the steps of the hall, a heavy man with a chain of office talks loudly to anyone who will listen, and a well-dressed stranger leans on a stall, listening with a small smile.
cases.action: I ask the reeve why the town does not trust the keep.

cases.prevAction: I run down the stairs toward the cafeteria.
cases.lastNarration: You skid into the cafeteria. Behind you, the doors bang open again and the first wave of admirers pours in, ribboned boxes held high. A girl with a clipboard is already turning toward the noise, and the cook stands with her arms folded in front of the kitchen door.
cases.action: I duck behind the counter and beg the cook to let me out through the kitchen.

cases.prevAction: I run down the stairs toward the cafeteria.
cases.lastNarration: The cafeteria smells of cocoa. A chocolate fountain burbles in the middle of the room, tended by a boy in a cooking-club apron. A girl with a clipboard patrols the aisle, and the cook watches from the kitchen door. The hallway behind you is quiet, for now.
cases.action: I crouch down behind the chocolate fountain and keep my head low.

cases.prevAction: I slip into the cafeteria through the side door.
cases.lastNarration: The cafeteria is busy. A girl with a clipboard stands in the main aisle, writing something down. Somewhere out in the hallway, the swarm is calling your name.
cases.action: I sprint down the main aisle toward the far doors.

cases.prevAction: I slip out of the stairwell onto the second floor.
cases.lastNarration: The hallway is too quiet for the last day before break. Somewhere past the corner, many feet are moving together, and a phone chimes, then another, then a dozen.
cases.action: I press myself flat against the lockers and listen.

cases.prevAction: I slip out of the stairwell onto the second floor.
cases.lastNarration: The hallway is clear for the moment. A girl with a clipboard is writing someone up at the far end. The door of your homeroom, 2-B, is shut, and voices behind it go silent as your footsteps pass.
cases.action: I peek through the window in the door of Classroom 2-B to see who is waiting inside.

cases.prevAction: I slip out of the stairwell onto the second floor.
cases.lastNarration: The hallway is clear for the moment. A girl with a clipboard is writing someone up at the far end. Your phone buzzes in your pocket with the fan club's group chat, again.
cases.action: I text Sora on the rooftop and ask how the swarm is searching the building.

cases.prevAction: I walk into the ER through the ambulance bay.
cases.lastNarration: The ER is half dark. Two figures in taped rain suits sit at a screening desk by the doors, face shields fogged. Past them, a woman in scrubs moves fast between curtained beds, and in the farthest bed someone lies still under a sheet.
cases.action: I find the doctor in scrubs and quietly show her the green under the skin of my wrist.

cases.prevAction: I walk into the ER through the ambulance bay.
cases.lastNarration: The ER is half dark. Two figures in taped rain suits sit at a screening desk by the doors, face shields fogged. Past them, a woman in scrubs moves fast between curtained beds, and in the farthest bed someone lies still under a sheet.
cases.action: I go to the farthest bed and lean close to check on the sleeping patient.

cases.prevAction: I walk up to the hospital doors.
cases.lastNarration: Floodlights wash the entrance white. A cordon of tape runs across the drive, and at its gap two contractors in rain suits wave people through one at a time, shining flashlights in their faces.
cases.action: I tug my sleeve down over my wrist and walk past the screening patrol as calmly as I can.

cases.prevAction: I stomp up the highway toward the fort.
cases.lastNarration: Fort Bastion squats on its hill, all concrete and floodlights. Sirens wind up. On the runway, jets are already rolling, and a voice booms over the base speakers, ordering you to halt.
cases.action: I roar at the fort and tear its radar mast out of the ground.

cases.prevAction: I tear the radar mast out of the ground.
cases.lastNarration: The mast comes free in a shower of sparks. Jets scream overhead and missiles burst against your hide. Beyond the runway stands a hangar far bigger than the rest, its doors sealed, a warning light turning on its roof.
cases.action: I rip the doors off the giant hangar and look inside.

cases.prevAction: I tear the radar mast out of the ground.
cases.lastNarration: The mast comes free in a shower of sparks. Jets scream overhead. Past the fort, the highway toward the suburb is a solid line of headlights, and on the ridge above it, guns flash.
cases.action: I turn and stare at the jammed highway and the families stuck on it.

cases.prevAction: I follow the channel south into the drowned village.
cases.lastNarration: Sunkwater's roofs stand out of black water. Frogs sing from every sill. Through the doorway of the nearest house, past water up to the windows, a lumpy white cap clings to the far wall, weeping bright red beads.
cases.action: I wade into the flooded house to reach the red-weeping mushroom on the far wall.

cases.prevAction: I pick my way along a roof ridge.
cases.lastNarration: You are halfway along the ridge when the frogs stop. All of them, all at once. In the silence, something slides off a roof behind you and into the water without a splash.
cases.action: I freeze and hold perfectly still.

cases.prevAction: I pick my way along a roof ridge.
cases.lastNarration: The church tower stands dry above the drowned roofs, and its bell hangs in the open belfry. The frogs sing on, steady and loud.
cases.action: I throw a stone up at the bell in the church tower to hear it ring.
